name: teaser
_doc: Teaser shot list — the edit order of release/demo_scenario.md §4, as data.
Run it with scripts/demo/shoot.py (list | pose <id> | shoot [ids]).
COORDS. Shots on the sealed sustain stage (location C, built by
scripts/demo/sustain_live.py build) carry REAL coords and are shootable as-is.
Shots in the open world (location B: real veins, cliffs, ravines) deliberately
carry NO camera pos — where a cliff-dive or a vein lands is picked on the day.
Workflow for those: fly the camera by hand or `cam_pose` it, screenshot, write the
pos back into this file, then `pose <id>` to confirm the framing before rolling.
Inventing coords here would ship confidently-wrong takes, so we do not.
Shots 06_fleet and 07_operator need a second source (a 3-4 bot scene / a terminal
split-screen) and are listed for completeness — shoot.py rolls the game side only.

shots.note: HOOK: bot steps off a ledge, MLG-waters itself, keeps 20 hp. SHOT LIVE on the mesa set: cleared corridor + red_sand pad y71 + wall ledge y91 at x=-342 (fall ~20 — the verified MLG envelope; 50-block falls KILL, stepped floors KILL). Stage: tp (console below); needs a water_bucket in the bag (honest console drop → auto-pickup). during pushes W over the edge. RE-FRAMED for splash legibility: the earlier take was narratively complete but the splash was sub-perceptual — the water lives ~3 ticks (the reflex scoops right after landing) and the old wide pose ([-330.5,84] + smooth 0.18) reached the floor ~0.3 s late. Camera now sits LOW and CLOSE INSIDE the pit on its WEST column (-341.5, 73.8), facing EAST (yaw -90) at the landing column: with walk_off.sh's 500 ms in-game W tap the bot drops into the 4-wide pit and lands at x≈-338.8 / y72 (measured 21:58, WATER_CLUTCH_PLACE in the journal), i.e. 2.7 blocks in front of this camera, 1.8 over the pad. NO track: a tracked camera (hz 8, smooth 0.35) was still looking up the shaft when the bot landed and tilted down only ~0.2 s later (take 22:07, 30 fps frame strip), while the water lives ~3 ticks — so the splash happened below the frame edge. Static pitch 34 puts the pad at frame centre; the bot enters from the top edge ~2 blocks above the pad and the whole place+scoop plays at centre. GEOMETRY (measured with a World.getBlock air-map from the camera client): the pit is only 4 wide (x -342..-339) and air from y72 to y77; east of x=-338 the ground is solid terracotta up to y77-78, so the first re-frame at (-334.5, 74.5) sat INSIDE the cliff (screenshot = block interiors) — any pose at pad height must be within x -342..-339.
console: execute in minecraft:overworld run tp bot_1 -341.5 92 -67.5 -90 15

shots.note: Over-the-shoulder as the HV prospector GUI flashes open. SHOT LIVE at the cleared glade. The GUI itself is NOT visible to the camera — record the BOT's own display in parallel for the insert (both clients usually share ONE sway output; swap which window is fullscreen via swaymsg). AFTER the take send close_screen: keep_open blocks ALL movement (goto timeouts, false vein-unreachable) until closed.
console: execute in minecraft:overworld run tp bot_1 -168.5 93 -50.5 -154 5

shots.note: High wide over the ridge butte: bot digs in and SINKS, leaving an open shaft mouth. SHOT LIVE on the mesa ridge film set: dig column (-343,-70), surface y123 — FULL-column-probe solidity first (a tail-truncated probe read cost one bot death at (-344,-71), open air past the crest edge). The iron marker was pre-moved onto the column in bot_1's mc_world.json: drill has NO target arg, it walks to the nearest cached vein x/z (mission payload inner key is params, NOT args — args is silently dropped). Mission MUST start via during AFTER recording begins: shoot.py fires bot cmds pre-record, descent is ~2 blocks/s and the bot vanishes before frame 1 (cost take 1).

In the cut: bot eats an ore chamber block by block, camera tracking from the alcove window. SHOT LIVE on the ore-CHAMBER film set inside the mesa fin: room (-347..-343, 104..107, -74..-68) joined to a window punched through the thin east cliff wall (solid at x=-341, open air from x=-339), walls/floor lined with iron_ore, invisible minecraft:light[level=15] fill lights. Behavior = MINE mission, NOT drill: drill EXCAVATE plans a ±8 anchor box and wanders off across barren rock — a static wall camera got exactly 1 broken block in 100 s (dead take). NO dry open-world site exists: every target vein sits below the y62 water table (GTCEu compiled defaults via javap, pack does not override; 999 console ore probes above y62 → 0 hits).

Navigator triptych (bridge / ladder / rim-veto refusal) — strict profile, low angle. SHOT LIVE (climb variant): bot on the mesa-gorge floor (~-336 79 -68), goto the ridge top → it stair-climbs the terracotta wall; first ~8 s usable before it exits frame. Bridge + rim-veto takes still TODO. Gap leg SHOT day 3 → 04b_gap.

Nav triptych, gap leg. SHOT LIVE: two floating stone platforms over the gorge east of the fin (A top y100 x -331..-327, B x from -321, z -73..-69; hoodoo clutter cleared with console fills). 4-gap take (04_nav_bridge.mp4): bot lays a cobble nub and hops. 5-gap take (04_nav_bridge2.mp4): bot builds a raised cobble step and sprint-BOOST-leaps the whole void — poster frame mid-air at t≈5 s. Drive with greedy_drive via during (standalone goto/goto_waypoint wedges — known gotcha). Rim-veto leg still TODO.

The sustain loop on the sealed stage: bot mines the patch, furnaces glow, ingots go to the bank. Low 3/4 from the SE — close enough that ore, furnaces and chest all READ (the first take was shot from [13,109,9] and the base was a grey speck in a forest). ONE plan owner: the during-loop's lap() does its own plan_start per lap; nothing else may (the old pre-record `bot` plan_start was removed). ROOT CAUSE of the ~90% frozen earlier takes (journal-proven): the stage held only 9 ore, the self-looping plan ate them in ~15 s, then the mine mission sat in SCAN ~114 s until SCAN_EXHAUSTED (r=32 spiral x 3 cycles). Fix = 25-block patch + 30 s laps in sustain_live.py (LAP_DWELL_S), so the host re-arms before the patch runs dry. loop 3 covers the 80 s roll rather than filling it exactly: 2 full 30 s laps + ~2/3 of the third, with ~3 s of lap staging each. Cut to the live windows motion_probe finds.
3-4 bots working different parts of one wide frame (hub region leases keep them apart). Needs the fleet staged first — see FLEET_PLAYBOOK.
Split-screen: the game half. A queued want lands and the bot leaves to dig it. Film the terminal half separately and sync on the Enter keypress.

Static wide on the base while the loop grinds — roll long and speed it up ~20x in the edit. No tracking: the frame must not drift under a timelapse, so the bot walks through a fixed frame instead of the camera chasing it.
